Calibrate the frequency threshold of the reference professions

Source: R/reference_professions.R
calibrate_reference_threshold.Rd

Measures how many doubly-coded postings the frequency rule needs to beat the similarity rule. On the codes with at least n_large postings with both codes, it draws subsamples of k of those postings and records how often the mode of the subsample equals the mode of all of them; the threshold is the smallest k whose agreement exceeds the agreement of the similarity reference with the full mode on the same codes.

Usage

calibrate_reference_threshold(
  postings,
  from_col,
  to_col,
  sim_reference,
  k_grid = c(1L, 2L, 3L, 5L, 10L, 20L, 50L),
  n_large = 200L,
  n_rep = 100L,
  seed = 1L,
  from_na = c("", "Unclassifiable"),
  to_na = c("", "Unclassifiable")
)

Arguments

postings

A data.frame with one row per posting and the columns from_col and to_col.

from_col, to_col

Names of the starting and arrival code columns.

sim_reference

A data.frame with columns code and sim_code (for example the output of build_reference_professions()): the similarity reference of each starting code.

k_grid

Integer vector of subsample sizes. Default c(1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 20, 50).

n_large

Minimum number of doubly-coded postings for a code to enter the calibration. Default 200.

n_rep

Number of subsamples per code and size. Default 100.

seed

Integer seed of the subsampling. The global RNG state is restored on exit.

from_na, to_na

Values of the two code columns that mean "no code".

Value

A list with:

curve

data.table with k, agreement (mean over codes of the share of subsamples whose mode equals the full mode), agreement_weighted (the same, weighted by doubly-coded postings) and n_codes.

similarity_agreement

Share of the calibration codes whose similarity reference equals the full mode.

n_min

The smallest k of k_grid with agreement strictly above similarity_agreement, or NA if none.

codes

data.table with one row per code with at least n_large doubly-coded postings: code, n_cocoded, code_modal, sim_code, included (it has a similarity reference) and the per-size agreements in columns k_<k>.

Details

Modes are computed as in build_esco_cp_crosswalk(): ties are resolved on the code (byte order), both for the full mode and for the subsample modes, so the calibration measures the rule as it is applied. Subsamples are drawn without replacement. Codes with at least n_large doubly-coded postings but no similarity reference are listed in codes with included = FALSE and do not enter either agreement. The comparison favours neither rule on the codes it uses; it does not measure the agreement of the two rules on the codes with few postings, where the threshold is applied.

Examples

set.seed(1)
postings <- data.table::data.table(
  from = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 300),
  to = c(sample(c("x", "y"), 300, TRUE, c(0.8, 0.2)),
         sample(c("y", "z"), 300, TRUE, c(0.6, 0.4)))
)
sim <- data.table::data.table(code = c("A", "B"), sim_code = c("x", "z"))
calibrate_reference_threshold(postings, "from", "to", sim, n_rep = 20)
#> $curve
#>        k agreement agreement_weighted n_codes
#>    <int>     <num>              <num>   <int>
#> 1:     1     0.575              0.575       2
#> 2:     2     0.950              0.950       2
#> 3:     3     0.750              0.750       2
#> 4:     5     0.875              0.875       2
#> 5:    10     1.000              1.000       2
#> 6:    20     0.950              0.950       2
#> 7:    50     0.950              0.950       2
#> 
#> $similarity_agreement
#> [1] 0.5
#> 
#> $n_min
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $codes
#>      code n_cocoded code_modal sim_code included   k_1   k_2   k_3   k_5  k_10
#>    <char>     <int>     <char>   <char>   <lgcl> <num> <num> <num> <num> <num>
#> 1:      A       300          x        x     TRUE  0.70   1.0   1.0  1.00     1
#> 2:      B       300          y        z     TRUE  0.45   0.9   0.5  0.75     1
#>     k_20  k_50
#>    <num> <num>
#> 1:   1.0   1.0
#> 2:   0.9   0.9
#>
